bugs.title: Idempotency key depends on the order of the payload's keys
bugs.description: getHashedIdempotencyKey() hashes JSON.stringify(payload) directly instead of JSON.stringify(deepSort(payload)). JSON.stringify keeps the object's own key order, so two payloads with the same content but keys in a different order produce different hashes and therefore different idempotency keys. getHashedPayload() still sorts, which makes the omission easy to miss.
bugs.runtime_failure: A retry of the same logical request whose JSON arrives with its keys in a different order (a different client or SDK version, a JSON library that orders keys differently, a proxy or queue that re-serialises the body, or code that builds the object field by field in another order) gets a new idempotency key. saveInProgress finds no record for that key, so the function runs again: duplicate side effects such as a second charge, a second order or a second message published.
bugs.conditions: Only when the key order differs between attempts. Byte-identical retries (the usual case in tests, and for a single client retrying its own request) still produce the same key, so the bug stays hidden until two serialisations meet. With eventKeyJmesPath selecting a single scalar value (for example an order id) the order does not matter and the bug cannot occur.
bugs.fix: Hash the canonical form again: JSON.stringify(deepSort(payload)), as getHashedPayload() does.

worsenings.title: Sorting an object copies it once per key
worsenings.description: sortObject builds its result with a spread inside reduce, so each step copies every key added so far. An object with k keys costs O(k²) work and allocations instead of O(k).
worsenings.when_it_matters: For large payloads with many keys (a whole API Gateway event, big nested bodies), on every invocation.
worsenings.better: Write into one accumulator (acc[key] = deepSort(object[key]); return acc), or Object.fromEntries(sortedKeys.map((k) => [k, deepSort(object[k])])).

rubric.point: First: getRecordIdentity, then saveInProgress (which writes an INPROGRESS record through _putRecord), the function runs, then saveSuccess (which writes the COMPLETED record and its result through _updateRecord).

Second: getRecordIdentity, then saveInProgress, whose _putRecord fails with IdempotencyItemAlreadyExistsError; the existing record is validated (processExistingRecord, or getRecord if the error carries none) and determineResultFromIdempotencyRecord returns the stored { status: 'ok' } without calling the function.
Payload validation (payloadValidationJmesPath) only takes part on the second call, when the stored record is compared with the new event.

search() selects 'A-1'; JSON.stringify gives the string "A-1" (with quotes), which is hashed (md5, base64) and prefixed: chargeFn#<hash>. The amount is not part of the key, so events for the same order share it.

If orderId is missing and throwOnNoIdempotencyKey is false, the handler skips idempotency for that call (shouldSkipIdempotency) and just runs the function; if it is true, getHashedIdempotencyKey throws IdempotencyKeyError.
With an empty eventKeyJmesPath the whole event is hashed instead, so any difference anywhere in the event gives a new key.
expiryTimestamp is 13:00:00 in seconds since the epoch; inProgressExpiryTimestamp is 12:00:30 in milliseconds since the epoch.
At 12:30 getStatus() returns INPROGRESS: it only checks expiryTimestamp, not the in-progress expiry. At 13:30 it returns EXPIRED.
Whether an abandoned in-progress record can be taken over is decided by the store's conditional write (stubs.ts), using the millisecond timestamp.
getHashedIdempotencyKey() hashes JSON.stringify(payload) without deepSort, so the key depends on the order of the payload's keys.
The same request serialised with a different key order gets a different key, no existing record is found, and the function runs again: duplicate side effects.
It only happens when the key order differs between attempts; byte-identical retries still deduplicate, so tests pass.
Fix: JSON.stringify(deepSort(payload)), as getHashedPayload() does.
Payload validation does not catch it: getHashedPayload() still sorts, but it only compares records found under the same key.

(Real upstream code, not the seeded bug.) determineResultFromIdempotencyRecord() compares inProgressExpiryTimestamp with new Date().getUTCMilliseconds(), which is 0-999 rather than the current time, so the "in progress expiry has passed" branch never runs.
A failed run must be retryable: deleting the record frees the key so the next attempt runs the function again; storing the failure would make every retry return the error until the record expired.
If the delete itself fails, IdempotencyPersistenceLayerError is thrown and the INPROGRESS record blocks the key until its in-progress expiry.
An INPROGRESS record can change elsewhere (completed or deleted by the invocation that owns it); a cached copy would keep this instance treating the key as in progress, or out of date.
COMPLETED records are safe to serve from memory until they expire, and getFromCache() drops expired ones.
The reduce builds a new object with { ...acc, [key]: ... } for every key, copying everything added so far: sorting an object with k keys costs O(k²) copies instead of O(k).
Mutate one accumulator instead (acc[key] = deepSort(object[key]); return acc;), or build it with Object.fromEntries over the sorted keys.
It runs on every invocation, on the whole payload (or the selected part), for the key and again for payload validation, so large events with many keys pay it on every request.

Today the second call gets IdempotencyAlreadyInProgressError. Better: wait and retry with backoff (or poll the record until it is COMPLETED) before failing, with the in-progress expiry tied to the function timeout.
Return a clear "in progress, retry later" response (for an API, 409 or 202 with Retry-After) and count these conflicts in metrics.

grader_notes: A line comment around persistence/BasePersistenceLayer.ts line 342 that explains the missing sort earns R8 to R10 even if Q4 is blank.
The getUTCMilliseconds() comparison in IdempotencyHandler.ts is real upstream code. Give R13 for spotting it; it is not a false positive and not the seeded bug.
